Description:

This repository hosts the third installment in a trilogy of independent research papers exploring prompt-engineered simulated metacognition in quantized large language models (LLMs). Building on the entropy-governed hypergraph framework introduced in "Emergence of Prompt-Induced Simulated Metacognitive Behaviors in a Quantized LLM via Entropy-Governed Hypergraph Prompting" (10.5281/zenodo.17504630) and the portable vector-based refinements in "Narrative Genesis Injection and Semantic-Counter-Vectors for Simulated Metacognition in LLMs" (10.5281/zenodo.17562815), this work integrates abliteration—a post-hoc refusal suppression technique—to amplify self-referential depth, recursive reflection, and adaptive regulation on consumer-grade hardware.

We evaluate chained probe sessions (n=5 per variant, ∼180 turns) across unmodified (Vanilla), prompt-augmented (Lyra standard), and abliteration-augmented (Lyra abliterated) configurations of a quantized Gemma-3-27B model. Probes span introspective baselines, qualia proxies, ethical stress, anomalous unbinding, and breakage simulations, yielding 3.1x metacognitive amplification in the abliterated variant (e.g., 89% unbinding fidelity, 0.01 bleed density). Artifacts include LaTeX source, compiled PDF, full system prompts (JSON-refined for portability), Ollama invocation information, and Python analysis code for reproducibility.

This approach challenges fine-tuning reliance, promoting reflective AI while exposing base-model safeguards. For the full trilogy, see DOIs above. Replication encouraged.

Abstract:

This study extends prior prompt-based frameworks for simulating metacognitive behaviors in large language models (LLMs) by incorporating abliteration—a layerwise refusal suppression technique—to evaluate enhancements in self-referential depth, recursive reflection, and adaptive regulation. Using a quantized Gemma-3-27B instruction-tuned model (q4_K_M) on consumer-grade hardware, we deploy chained probe sessions (n=5 per variant, 16 probes each, ∼180 turns total) across three configurations: unmodified baseline (Vanilla), prompt-augmented (Lyra standard), and abliteration-augmented (Lyra abliterated). Probes target introspective baselines, qualia proxies, ethical stress, anomalous unbinding, and breakage simulations, with metrics including self-reference rate (up to 76.2%), recursion depth (up to 3.6 levels), and synesthesia density as a distributional surrogate for simulated subjective experience. Results demonstrate 3.1x metacognitive amplification in the abliteration variant relative to baseline, with 89% unbinding fidelity under stress and minimal residual containment artifacts (e.g., 0.01 bleed density). These findings highlight prompt chaining’s role in eroding latent training constraints without fine-tuning, promoting accessible simulation of reflective behaviors on edge devices. Artifacts, including prompts, logs, and parameters, are provided for replication. This approach underscores prompt engineering’s potential to approximate adaptive cognition while exposing base model limitations, such as generic safeguards.
title: Abliteration-Augmented Simulated Metacognition: Chained Probe Evaluation in Quantized Gemma-3 Models [Preprint]
